body: Race condition: a backup code can be used more than once. The code reads `user.backupCodes`, checks for a match in memory, then writes the new encrypted blob back with no concurrency guard. Two concurrent sign-ins with the same code both pass the `indexOf` check and both succeed. The last write also wins, so a code burned by one request can come back if another request consumes a different code at the same time. Consume the code atomically, e.g. a transaction with a conditional update on the previous `backupCodes` value (optimistic lock), and fail if no row was updated.

The backup code is burned here, before the rest of `authorize` runs (e.g. `validateRole` and later checks). If a later step rejects the login, the user has lost a code and is still not logged in. Also, `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll` will throw on unexpected input, and the comparison is not constant-time. Consider hashing codes (e.g. store hashes instead of an encrypted list) and comparing with `timingSafeEqual`.

In an API route, `throw new Error(...)` returns an unhandled 500 with no JSON body, so the client falls through to a generic error. The existing TOTP branch has the same problem. Return `res.status(500).json({ error: ErrorCode.InternalServerError })` instead, as setup.ts does. Also, `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` on line 61 crashes if `backupCode` is not a string (e.g. a number in the JSON body). Validate the type first.

Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have `backupCodes = null`. In both login and disable they hit `MissingBackupCodes`, and nothing lets them generate codes short of disabling and re-enabling 2FA. So the 'Lost access' button is shown to existing users but can never work for them. Consider hiding it when no codes exist, or adding a way to regenerate codes. Also, once all 10 codes are used there is no way to regenerate them either.

At the DisplayBackupCodes step, 2FA is already enabled on the server, but `onEnable()` only runs from the Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog with Esc or an overlay click (`onOpenChange`), `utils.viewer.me` is never invalidated, so the switch still shows 2FA as disabled. The modal state also isn't reset (`step` stays DisplayBackupCodes), so reopening shows the old backup codes screen. Handle `onOpenChange` at this step the same way as Close (`resetState(); onEnable();`), and revoke the blob URL there too.

`backupCodesUrl` is revoked only when setup runs again, and the check reads a possibly stale state value. The blob URL, which holds the plaintext backup codes, is never revoked when the dialog closes or the component unmounts. `resetState` also doesn't clear `backupCodes`/`backupCodesUrl`, so the plaintext codes stay in component state after closing. Clear and revoke them in `resetState`.

Putting a `<Button>` (a `<button>`) inside an `<a>` is invalid interactive nesting. It hurts accessibility and some browsers handle the click inconsistently. Use the Button's `href` prop, or render the anchor styled as a button.

Cancel (and closing the dialog through `onOpenChange`) doesn't reset `twoFactorLostAccess` or the form. When the modal is reopened it still shows the backup code input and the previously typed password or codes. Call `setTwoFactorLostAccess(false); resetForm();` on cancel/close.
Copy-paste leftover: this component is exported as `TwoFactor`, the same name as the real TwoFactor component. Stack traces and React DevTools will be confusing. Rename it to `BackupCode`.
